description: Hi! I'm an Electronics & Systems student passionate about hardware, robotics, and AI. My core skills include Python, Arduino, ESP32, and 3D modeling (CATIA). I'm planning to work on either the 'Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer' or the 'Space Mission Design Game'. While I'm prepared to build the prototype solo, I'd love to welcome members skilled in Storytelling, Graphic Design, or Video Editing to round out the project.
summary: ORION-KID: Lunar Rescue Mission is an interactive hardware-software mission trainer designed to inspire and educate young learners about lunar landing physics and space exploration. Built in Python (Pygame) and paired with a custom ESP32 physical controller featuring tactile push buttons, LED status indicators, an LCD telemetry screen, a DHT11 environmental sensor, and an audio feedback speaker communicating over Wi-Fi (UDP), the system bridges digital simulation with hands-on astronaut training. Players guide Captain Orion's lunar lander safely to the Moon's surface by managing thrust, timing, and environmental telemetry under realistic lunar gravity. By transforming complex orbital and descent mechanics into an intuitive, tactile arcade experience, ORION-KID makes space science accessible, engaging, and memorable for junior astronauts.
details:
What It Does & How It Works:

ORION-KID: Lunar Rescue Mission is an interactive hardware-software mission simulator designed to train junior astronauts in lunar landing mechanics and spaceflight telemetry. The system consists of two synchronized layers:

  1. Physical Mission Control Console (Hardware): Powered by an ESP32 microcontroller operating as a local Wi-Fi access point, equipped with three tactile push buttons (for thrust, confirmation, and mission responses), three status LEDs (visualizing safe landing windows and alerts), an LCD display showing live mission telemetry, a DHT11 sensor monitoring cabin/environmental temperature and humidity, and an 8-ohm speaker for audio alerts.
  2. Lunar Lander Simulation (Software): Built in Python using Pygame, the simulation communicates bidirectionally with the ESP32 in real time over UDP (ports 4210 and 4211). Players guide Captain Orion's spacecraft under realistic lunar gravity (1.62 m/s²), managing thruster bursts and responding to physical LED/LCD prompts to achieve a soft touchdown.

Benefits, Creativity & Intended Impact:

Traditional space education relies heavily on passive reading or screen-only games. By combining tactile embedded hardware with an engaging arcade simulation, ORION-KID mirrors how real astronauts train using physical flight consoles. Key design considerations included low-latency wireless UDP communication, clear visual/auditory cues for young learners, and accessible, low-cost open-source components so classrooms and makerspaces can easily replicate the trainer.

Tools, Languages & Hardware Used:

  • Software & Languages: Python 3, Pygame, C++ (Arduino Framework for ESP32), UDP Socket Networking, Visual Studio Code, OBS Studio.
  • Hardware: ESP32 Development Board, DHT11 Temperature & Humidity Sensor, I2C LCD Display, Tactile Push Buttons, Status LEDs, 8Ω 0.25W Speaker.
